title: Shape concavities of 100 µm or more persist in developing stem cell aggregates

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Shape concavities of 100 µm or more persist in developing stem cell aggregates

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Aggregates of developing Xenopus pluripotent cells tend to close small gaps in their geometry; concavities 100 µm wide or more (12% of body length) gave stable long-term deformations, setting the minimal buildable feature size.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Materials and Methods › Build Filter.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Preliminary work determined that concavities with a width of 100 µm or greater (12% of total body length) produced stable long-term deformations suitable for biological building (SI Appendix, Fig. S7).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Materials and Methods › Build Filter.”. Scope: Reaggregated Xenopus laevis animal-cap tissue shaped by microsurgery

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric predictor and persistence outcome are directly measurable. Public supplementary observations can support the approximate threshold, but available coverage is unlikely to estimate a robust universal minimum feature size.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure initial concavity width and normalized body length from construction images, then model long-term persistence versus closure to estimate the feature-size threshold and uncertainty.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw longitudinal shape measurements may not be downloadable.

The threshold is based on preliminary work with limited samples.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.96

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Concavity width and persistence are direct morphometric variables with a clear threshold. The published support is a preliminary supplementary figure, not an open table of widths and outcomes. Confirming or refuting the 100 micrometer cutoff requires those measurements or a new build series.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Shape animal-cap aggregates with concavities of graded width and record whether each gap remains after a fixed culture interval; the size threshold holds if gaps at or above 100 micrometers persist and smaller gaps close.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The result is described as preliminary work in a supplement figure, without a deposited morphometry table.

Testing it again requires new microsurgical aggregates.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data existence: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.3
